en.greeting: Hi! Today is all about real conversations: telling someone about your weekend, sharing your plans, and keeping the chat going. You already know the grammar, so let's use it.

steps.title: How was your weekend?
steps.text: Let's start with the two questions people ask every Monday.
steps.body: **How was your weekend?** asks if it was good: answer **It was** + a word: *It was great! It was OK.* or **Not bad.** **What did you do?** asks what happened: answer with **past verbs**: *I went to Puncak. I stayed at home.* **The trap:** Indonesian doesn't change the verb (*Minggu lalu saya pergi…*), so learners say *Last weekend I go…*. In English the weekend is over, so **every verb is past**: went, ate, stayed.

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: It's Monday morning. A colleague asks you something. Press play.

question.prompt: Listen to the question. Which answer is correct?
question.listen: What did you do on Saturday?
options: I visit my grandma in Depok.
I'm going to visit my grandma in Depok.
I visited my grandma in Depok.
question.explanation: The question uses **did** and Saturday is over, so answer in the past: **I visited**. *I visit* is the Indonesian habit (no past form), and *I'm going to visit* is a plan for later.

steps.title: Add a detail
steps.text: One sentence is a good start. Now make your story a little longer.
steps.body: Add **who** (*with my family, on my own* = sendirian), **where** (*to Ancol, at a warung*) and **what it was like**: **It was** + a describing word (*fun, delicious, crowded, tiring*). **Seru** is **fun**, not *funny* (funny = lucu). **Macet** is *The traffic was terrible.* Join ideas with **and**, **but**, **because**: *We went to Ancol, but it was very crowded.*

steps.title: Monday at the office
steps.text: Here are some short weekend stories. Each one has a detail. Read them out loud.
steps.body: **It was tiring** = the trip made you tired. **I was tired** = you were tired. Both are fine, but not *It was tired*.

examples.en: I went to Ancol with my kids. It was fun, but very crowded.
examples.id: Saya ke Ancol sama anak-anak. Seru, tapi ramai banget.

examples.en: We ate nasi padang at a warung near the station. It was delicious.
examples.id: Kami makan nasi padang di warung dekat stasiun. Enak banget.

examples.en: I went to Bandung on my own. The traffic was terrible!
examples.id: Saya ke Bandung sendirian. Macetnya parah!

examples.en: It was OK. I didn't go out because I was tired.
examples.id: Biasa aja. Saya nggak ke mana-mana karena capek.

examples.en: How was your holiday? — Great! I went back to my hometown for Lebaran.
examples.id: Liburanmu gimana? — Seru! Saya mudik waktu Lebaran.

steps.title: Past or future?
steps.text: The time word in the question tells you which form to use.

timeline.title: Last weekend → this weekend
timeline.caption: Last weekend and yesterday are finished: past (I went, It was great). This weekend is coming: going to, or I'm + -ing for something fixed with other people.

steps.title: Your plans
steps.text: On Friday, the question moves to the future.
steps.body: **What are you going to do this weekend?** → your own plan: **I'm going to** + verb: *I'm going to visit my aunt.* **What are you doing on Saturday?** → something fixed with other people: **I'm** + verb-**ing** + a time: *I'm meeting Sari at 7.* No plans? **Nothing special.** / **I'm not sure.** **The trap:** *Besok saya ke Bogor* has no future in the verb, so learners say *Tomorrow I go to Bogor*. Say **Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor.**

pairs.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
What are you doing on Saturday?

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Match your answer to the question: plan or past?

question.prompt: It's Friday afternoon. Dimas asks: 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Which answer is correct?
options: I going to wash my motorbike.
I'm going to wash my motorbike.
question.explanation: Dimas asks about a plan, so use **am + going to + verb**: *I'm going to wash*. *I going to* is missing **am** (Indonesian *mau* has no 'be'), and *I washed* is the past: the weekend hasn't happened yet.

steps.title: Follow-up questions
steps.text: People often ask one more question. Give a little more than yes or no.
steps.body: Answer with the **short answer** + **one more fact**: *Was it expensive?* — **No, it wasn't.** *It was only 50,000 rupiah.* The short answer copies the first word: **Did** → *I did / I didn't*, **Was** → *it was / it wasn't*. Then **ask back**: *How about you? Where did you go? Who did you go with?* Indonesian *sama siapa* comes at the end, and so does English **with**. Watch the order: *Where did you go?*, not *Where you went?*

pairs.en: Did you have a good time?

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: You just came back from a trip to Yogyakarta. Your friend asks about it. Press play.

question.prompt: Listen to your friend's question. Choose the best reply.
question.listen: Did you have a good time in Yogyakarta?
options: Yes, I do! We visit Borobudur.
Yes, I did! We visited Borobudur and ate gudeg.
No, I didn't. It was really fun!
question.explanation: A **did** question gets **Yes, I did**, plus one more fact in the past: *We visited… and ate…*. *Yes, I do* and *We visit* are the present, and *No, I didn't… It was really fun!* says two opposite things.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: Your colleague had dinner with someone last night. Ask who.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamu makan malam sama siapa?
question.solution: Who did you have dinner with?
question.explanation: Question word + **did** + you + base verb: **have**, not *had*, because did already shows the past. Indonesian *sama siapa* is at the end, and English **with** goes at the end too.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole conversation on one page. Keep it for Monday morning.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Weekend chat: past & plans
artifact.intro: The questions you'll hear, and how to answer: answer, add a detail, ask back.
rows: It was great / OK. Not bad.
I went to… / I stayed at home.
With my family. / On my own.
Did you have a good time?
Yes, I did! + one more fact
No, it wasn't. + one more fact
What are you going to do this weekend?
What are you doing on Saturday?
tips: Finished time (last weekend, yesterday) → **every** verb is past: **I went**, not `I go`.
**Did** question → **Yes, I did / No, I didn't** + one more fact.

examples.id: Seru! Saya ke Bogor sama keluarga. Kamu sendiri?

examples.en: Was it expensive? — No, it wasn't. The hotel was only 300,000 rupiah.
examples.id: Mahal nggak? — Nggak. Hotelnya cuma 300.000 rupiah.

examples.en: Nothing special. I'm going to relax at home.
examples.id: Nggak ada yang spesial. Saya mau santai di rumah.

steps.title: Watch and listen
steps.text: Want more? Watch a short chat with reactions and listen to people talking about their weekend.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita fokus ke percakapan sungguhan: cerita tentang akhir pekanmu, menyampaikan rencana, dan menjaga obrolan tetap jalan. Tata bahasanya sudah kamu tahu, jadi ayo kita pakai.

steps.title: How was your weekend?
steps.text: Kita mulai dari dua pertanyaan yang ditanyakan orang setiap hari Senin.
steps.body: **How was your weekend?** menanyakan rasanya: jawab **It was** + satu kata: *It was great! It was OK.* atau **Not bad.** **What did you do?** menanyakan apa yang terjadi: jawab dengan **kata kerja lampau**: *I went to Puncak. I stayed at home.* **Jebakannya:** bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja (*Minggu lalu saya pergi…*), jadi pelajar bilang *Last weekend I go…*. Dalam bahasa Inggris akhir pekannya sudah lewat, jadi **semua kata kerjanya lampau**: went, ate, stayed.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Senin pagi. Rekan kerjamu bertanya sesuatu. Tekan play.

question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaannya. Jawaban mana yang benar?
question.listen: What did you do on Saturday?
options: I visit my grandma in Depok.
I'm going to visit my grandma in Depok.
I visited my grandma in Depok.
question.explanation: Pertanyaannya memakai **did** dan hari Sabtu sudah lewat, jadi jawab dengan bentuk lampau: **I visited**. *I visit* adalah kebiasaan dari bahasa Indonesia (tanpa bentuk lampau), dan *I'm going to visit* adalah rencana untuk nanti.

steps.title: Tambahkan detail
steps.text: Satu kalimat sudah bagus untuk mulai. Sekarang buat ceritamu sedikit lebih panjang.
steps.body: Tambahkan **siapa** (*with my family, on my own* = sendirian), **di mana** (*to Ancol, at a warung*) dan **bagaimana rasanya**: **It was** + kata sifat (*fun, delicious, crowded, tiring*). **Seru** itu **fun**, bukan *funny* (funny = lucu). **Macet** itu *The traffic was terrible.* Gabungkan ide dengan **and**, **but**, **because**: *We went to Ancol, but it was very crowded.*

steps.title: Senin di kantor
steps.text: Ini beberapa cerita akhir pekan yang pendek. Masing-masing punya detail. Baca dengan suara keras.
steps.body: **It was tiring** = perjalanannya bikin capek. **I was tired** = kamu merasa capek. Dua-duanya benar, tapi bukan *It was tired*.

steps.title: Masa lalu atau masa depan?
steps.text: Kata waktu di pertanyaannya memberi tahu bentuk mana yang dipakai.

timeline.title: Akhir pekan lalu → akhir pekan ini
timeline.caption: Akhir pekan lalu dan kemarin sudah selesai: bentuk lampau (I went, It was great). Akhir pekan ini belum datang: going to, atau I'm + -ing untuk acara yang sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain.

steps.title: Rencanamu
steps.text: Hari Jumat, pertanyaannya pindah ke masa depan.
steps.body: **What are you going to do this weekend?** → rencanamu sendiri: **I'm going to** + kata kerja: *I'm going to visit my aunt.* **What are you doing on Saturday?** → acara yang sudah dijadwalkan dengan orang lain: **I'm** + kata kerja-**ing** + waktu: *I'm meeting Sari at 7.* Belum ada rencana? **Nothing special.** / **I'm not sure.** **Jebakannya:** *Besok saya ke Bogor* tidak menunjukkan masa depan di kata kerjanya, jadi pelajar bilang *Tomorrow I go to Bogor*. Katakan **Tomorrow I'm going to Bogor.**

pairs.en: What are you going to do this weekend?
What are you doing on Saturday?

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sesuaikan jawabanmu dengan pertanyaannya: rencana atau masa lalu?

question.prompt: Jumat sore. Dimas bertanya: 'What are you going to do this weekend?' Jawaban mana yang benar?
options: I going to wash my motorbike.
I'm going to wash my motorbike.
question.explanation: Dimas menanyakan rencana, jadi pakai **am + going to + kata kerja**: *I'm going to wash*. *I going to* tidak punya **am** (kata *mau* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya 'be'), dan *I washed* itu masa lalu: akhir pekannya belum terjadi.

steps.title: Pertanyaan lanjutan
steps.text: Orang sering bertanya satu kali lagi. Jawab sedikit lebih dari ya atau tidak.
steps.body: Jawab dengan **jawaban singkat** + **satu fakta lagi**: *Was it expensive?* — **No, it wasn't.** *It was only 50,000 rupiah.* Jawaban singkat mengikuti kata pertama pertanyaannya: **Did** → *I did / I didn't*, **Was** → *it was / it wasn't*. Lalu **tanya balik**: *How about you? Where did you go? Who did you go with?* *Sama siapa* ada di akhir, dan **with** dalam bahasa Inggris juga di akhir. Perhatikan urutannya: *Where did you go?*, bukan *Where you went?*

pairs.en: Did you have a good time?

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Kamu baru pulang dari Yogyakarta. Temanmu bertanya tentang perjalananmu. Tekan play.

question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan temanmu. Pilih jawaban terbaik.
question.listen: Did you have a good time in Yogyakarta?
options: Yes, I do! We visit Borobudur.
Yes, I did! We visited Borobudur and ate gudeg.
No, I didn't. It was really fun!
question.explanation: Pertanyaan **did** dijawab dengan **Yes, I did**, ditambah satu fakta lagi dalam bentuk lampau: *We visited… and ate…*. *Yes, I do* dan *We visit* itu bentuk sekarang, dan *No, I didn't… It was really fun!* mengatakan dua hal yang berlawanan.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Tadi malam rekan kerjamu makan malam dengan seseorang. Tanyakan dengan siapa.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kamu makan malam sama siapa?
question.solution: Who did you have dinner with?
question.explanation: Kata tanya + **did** + you + kata kerja dasar: **have**, bukan *had*, karena did sudah menunjukkan masa lalu. *Sama siapa* ada di akhir kalimat bahasa Indonesia, dan **with** dalam bahasa Inggris juga di akhir.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh percakapannya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk Senin pagi.
